# Bundled WPE source and downstream patch policy

`upstream.json` pins the WPE WebKit **2.54.0 release archive** by URL and SHA-256.
It does not assert an unverified upstream Git commit. `patches/series` lists
reviewable downstream patches in application order. The series includes a WPE
clipboard failure-handling fix and opt-in extension embedding APIs described below.

Permitted patches provide generic embedding capabilities. Public APIs, source,
tests and patch subjects must not contain application/extension-specific concepts.
UXP is never part of this series. Record each patch's purpose, upstream base,
changed files, added API, default/unopted behavior, tests and upstreamability in
this directory. No manual unlisted edits to the extracted WebKit source are allowed.

## Verify

```sh
python3 tools/wpe/test-verify-source.py
python3 tools/wpe/verify-source.py --allow-python-cache
```

Verification first checks the pinned archive hash. It constructs expected patched
files from the archive in a temporary directory, applies the series with
`git apply --check` and `git apply`, and compares every source entry. Contents,
executable bits, symlink targets, deleted files and unexpected additions are
checked. Unlisted or duplicate patches fail. Symlink/gitlink and binary patches
are deliberately unsupported. Source under test is never repaired or modified.

The release archive repeats some paths; the last member at a path wins, matching
normal extraction. This is not an allowance for edits in the source tree.

The optional flag allows generated `__pycache__/name.cpython-N[.opt-N].pyc` files
only when their source `.py` module is itself in the verified inventory. No source
file is excluded. Without that flag, these generated extras fail verification too.
The build wrapper sets `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` to the object directory, so it neither
uses those pre-existing source-side caches nor generates new caches in the vendor
tree. Generated bytecode is not a downstream source patch or shipped runtime file.

## Reproduce a patched source directory

An enabled `./mach build` prepares a missing source cache automatically through
`tools/wpe/prepare-source.py`: download, verify the pinned hash, extract into a
temporary directory, apply the listed patches, and publish the completed tree.
An existing source directory must match its recorded patch series. When that
series changes, preparation verifies the old tree, constructs the new tree from
the pinned archive, and replaces only differing files. Unlisted edits are rejected.
A shared source lock protects compilation; preparation holds the exclusive lock.
The adjacent series-state JSON records exact patch contents for verification of
old caches. An interrupted update that leaves mixed contents fails verification;
it is not silently accepted or repaired. Configure
never downloads or builds WebKit. Build outputs live in `OBJDIR/webkit`; see
[the build integration](../../docs/wpe-runtime-packaging.md).

For manual source preparation:

Verify the archive hash against `upstream.json`, extract it into a **new** working
directory, then apply the listed patches in order with `git apply` from that source
root. Use absolute paths to each patch. Run the verifier with `--source` pointing
to the resulting directory. Do not reapply patches to an already modified tree,
reverse arbitrary edits to make a check pass, or overwrite a running build's files.

`tools/wpe/build-runtime.py` runs this verification before configuring/building or
installing. `--source-archive` can select another local copy of the **same pinned
archive**. Updating the upstream version is an explicit pin/series review.

The verifier establishes source provenance, not binary reproducibility or runtime
correctness. A new patch still requires build, upstream-style API tests, embedding
integration tests, race/timeout tests and pre-fetch server-counter tests. No such
broker success is claimed by a passing source audit.

## 0001: failed WPE clipboard text reads

Base: WPE WebKit 2.54.0. No new API or embedding opt-in. The public
`wpe_clipboard_read_text` now initializes its size output before argument guards.
`WebPasteboardProxy::readText` initializes the length and returns an empty string
on a failed read instead of constructing a span from a null pointer and potentially
uninitialized length. Valid text reads retain their existing behavior.

Changed files: `Source/WebKit/WPEPlatform/wpe/WPEClipboard.cpp` and
`Source/WebKit/UIProcess/wpe/WebPasteboardProxyWPE.cpp`. This is a generic WPE
bug fix suitable for upstream submission; it contains no application concepts.
The September 28 crash dump resolves to `WTFCrash` from the string-length
assertion in `StringImpl::create`, called by `WebPasteboardProxy::readText`.
Only code addresses were examined; no clipboard contents were logged.

Validation: rebuilt WPE, verified all 38,842 source entries against the archive
and patch series, then rebuilt/staged the application runtime. The standalone
`tools/wpe/clipboard-api.c` exercises valid, absent, cleared and invalid-format
reads through the public API (the invalid-format GLib diagnostic is expected).
The native `input` fixture uses real Ctrl+V events and dummy ASCII, Unicode and
empty clipboard values in a password input on an isolated X display.

## 0002–0005: extension embedding APIs

All four patches target the pinned WPE WebKit 2.54.0 source. These are downstream
embedding interfaces; no upstream acceptance is claimed.

* **0002** adds `webkit_web_view_set_resource_policy_enabled` and a preference
  that defaults to false. Enabled NetworkProcess loads send attributed request,
  redirect, response, and completion messages to the embedder. Pending decisions
  preserve the original transport request and expire after 30 seconds. Missing,
  malformed, expired, and rejected decisions block the pending load. The patch
  changes network load parameters, the network loader, UI process messaging,
  GLib WebView API, and preference definitions.
* **0003** adds synchronous extension-to-view messaging, frame parent IDs,
  frame user-origin stylesheets, and `webkit_web_page_add_user_script` for
  document-start/end scripts in the extension's actual `WebKitScriptWorld`.
  A separately created world with the same name is not the same realm.
  It changes WebPageProxy messaging and the GLib
  web-process extension API. A synchronous recipient must not synchronously call
  back into the blocked WebProcess. Messaging times out after ten seconds.
* **0004** applies deferred policy before WebSocket task creation. It carries
  document/frame attribution through socket IPC and handles closing a pending
  socket. Unopted views retain immediate socket creation.
* **0005** adds a GLib web-page `resource-policy` signal before asynchronous and
  synchronous resource dispatch, allowing extension code in the WebProcess to
  consult its local content-policy callbacks. It shares resource classification
  with NetworkProcess policy. It is gated by the same opt-in preference.

Source-verifier and patch-update tests cover provenance, revision/removal of
patches, preservation of unchanged file timestamps, and rejection of unrelated
source edits. The managed WPE/application build, strict unchanged uBlock 1.16.6.1
audit, and generic installed-XUL-addon fixture have passed. The latter includes
pending-request cancellation and suspension/resumption of a POST without changing
its body. See [coverage and remaining compatibility gaps](../../docs/content-engine-legacy/ublock-adapter.md).
These checks do not establish universal XUL compatibility or replace upstream
API, concurrency, timeout, and security testing.

## 0006: trusted isolated-world DOM access

`webkit_script_world_set_cross_origin_access` explicitly grants DOM access to
trusted embedding code in an isolated world. The normal page world cannot be
granted this capability. A weak set tracks opted-in worlds; document origins,
network CORS, and unopted worlds retain their normal checks. Basilisk opts in
only its privileged extension API world, never ordinary userscript sandboxes.
This permits shared extension modules to observe and act on subdocuments without
changing the web page's same-origin policy. The Greasemonkey fixture checks both
cross-origin subframe injection and denial of cross-origin reads from page code
and userscripts. The patch adds a private WebCore header and the GLib API and
modifies binding access checks; it does not modify DOMWrapperWorld layout.
